name: repression
description: An unconscious refusal to accept an internal memory or thought in order to avoid painful feelings.
perceptions: There's something unpleasant in my past.
It would be better if it didn't exist.
desires: desire to feel better about yourself
examples: Refusing to think about a traumatic event from your childhood.

guidance.description: 15 Signs You’re Repressing Trauma & What To Do About It

It may not be easy to find out why your unconscious has activated a defense mechanism. Some approaches include prayer, meditation, and therapy. None of them will work without a humble attitude and a real willingness to face something difficult.

comparisons.description: 'Denial' is refusal to accept external perceptions. 'Repression' is refusal to accept internal memories or thoughts.

variations.name: intellectualization
variations.description: An unconscious refusal to accept the emotional content of an experience while dealing with the rational aspect.
perceptions: I can't handle the emotional aspect of this outcome.
But I can deal with the everyday paperwork.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
desire to feel better about yourself
results: Not processing the emotional part of something traumatic.
examples: Throwing yourself into funeral arrangements without starting to deal with the grief.
A crime victim talks about statistics and motivations without handling the emotional impact.

comparisons.description: With 'intellectualization', you repress only the emotional aspect of the event. With 'repression', the whole thing is buried.

guidance.description: Signs You’re Intellectualizing Instead of Feeling Your Feelings

variations.name: compartmentalization
variations.description: Unconsciously switching between different mindsets to reduce anxiety from dissonance.
perceptions: There are multiple parts of my life that don't fit well together.
It's best I keep them separate.
desires: desire to be perceived a certain way
desire to feel better about yourself
results: This may be a mature way of dealing with a complex life, or it may cause problems over time.
examples: First responders who deal with trauma but want to have a peaceful home life.
Someone who's bisexual but also part of an intolerant religious community.

guidance.description: How to Compartmentalize to Reduce Stress - Creating boundaries to stop stress from taking over your life

commentaries.quote: Repression can be thought of as 'motivated forgetting': the active but unconscious 'forgetting' of unacceptable drives, emotions, ideas, or memories.
Unexpressed emotions will never die. They are buried alive and will come forth later in uglier ways.
The attempt to escape from pain, is what creates more pain.
It's people who are repressed and cannot express their fears that are dangerous.

In some cases, it can be fine to put off an emotional burden for a short time—it may even be necessary. But if emotions aren’t addressed over time, they can build up and interfere with daily life or escape in an unhealthy way, such as through anxiety or a panic attack.
